key_insight: A nonconforming finite element method can solve the surface biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces using only vertex values and scalar edge moments, avoiding both stabilization and Piola transforms.
engineering_relevance: This makes surface PDE discretization simpler to assemble and more practical for computational geometry and shell-like surface models while retaining provable stability and accuracy.
method: Uses a reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element with a purely local construction on each triangle of a piecewise planar surface.
Forms the bilinear operator from elementwise Laplacian inner products, enabling standard finite element assembly.
Proves weak discrete Miranda--Talenti-type estimates to establish stability on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on three surfaces that confirm the predicted first-order energy convergence and second-order broken H1 and L2 convergence, and it examines discrete Miranda--Talenti constants and angle-defect scaling.
watch_item: The stability guarantee depends on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes, so coarse meshes or poor geometric approximation may weaken performance.
paper_title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
